name: og-07-ecology-before-luca
title: Ecology before LUCA (Campaign VII)
question: In connected pore networks with cross-feeding, parasitism, cooperation and horizontal exchange, what emergent capabilities arise — compared to ancestral reconstructions, without assuming LUCA is primitive?
hypothesis: Heterogeneous populations develop metabolic diversity, cross-feeding and robustness single compartments do not; the emergent capability set overlaps the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction as a boundary.
objective: Run heterogeneous populations over shared spatial fields; compare emergent capabilities to LUCA reconstructions as a constraint.
proposed_models_methods: Vivarium multi-agent composites over shared spatial fields

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: cross-feeding-robustness
behavior_tests.description: Populations beat single compartments on diversity + robustness.

behavior_tests.name: luca-capability-overlap
behavior_tests.description: Emergent capabilities overlap the LUCA reconstruction (as a constraint).

pass_if.detail: overlap reported as a boundary, not a target

literature_anchors.expectation: LUCA: anaerobic, H2-dependent, CO2-fixing, FeS-rich (355 protein families)
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Not yet measurable — module processes not built

key_assumptions: Use LUCA as a constraint on capabilities eventually acquired, not evidence the first replicators were LUCA-like.
expert_questions: Scope og-07 to cross-feeding only first, or include horizontal exchange + parasitism from the start?
